title: The Jammed Wagon Gate
prompt: A rusted pin has seized the troupe's spare wagon gate half-open. Abenthy taps it: "Iron remembers fire, lad. Find the heat, bind it true, and the pin will let go." Choose where the energy comes from.

link.label: An iron nail heated in the fire

success_text: The pin creaks, glows dull orange, and lets go. The gate swings wide and the wagon rolls clear.

title: The Swollen Supply Hatch
prompt: Rain has swollen the wagon's supply hatch until the latch will not draw. A drop of sympathy — a whisper of heat along the hasp — should open it without splitting the wood.

link.label: A coin warmed between your hands

target.label: The iron hasp of the hatch

success_text: The hasp expands with a soft tick and the latch slips free. The hatch swings open on its own.

title: Boulder on the Track
prompt: A fallen boulder hems the wagons against the cut bank. There is a rain-crack running through its heart. Abenthy's trick: hammer in an iron wedge, feed real fire into it, and let the stone do the breaking for you.

link.label: The iron wedge seated in the crack

target.label: The water-seamed crack in the stone

effect.label: Fire the wedge and split the stone

success_text: The wedge glows, the crack hisses steam, and with a crack like a struck bell half the boulder sloughs away from the track.

title: The Cold Lamp
prompt: The lamp by the Waystone's door has gone cold, and the man behind the bar looks like he would rather not get up for it. The dying coals still remember fire. Bind that remembrance into the wick.

link.label: The lamp's brass handle — metal, like the poker left in the coals

success_text: The wick takes without being asked, flame standing up straight and yellow. Nobody in the room notices. That is rather the point.

title: A Fire to Stay Alive
prompt: Night is coming and there is no one left to strike a flint for you. Your hands remember your father's lessons. Sympathy needs a source of heat — even the small heat you can make yourself.

sources.label: Friction from your own two hands
Sun-warmed heartwood from the dead campfire's stack

link.label: A charred twig from last night's fire

success_text: Your palms burn with the effort and the pit takes anyway — a thread of orange in the gathering dark. You feed it like it is the only living thing left, because tonight, for you, it nearly is.
